title: Moralistic Fallacy
description:
When the conclusion expresses what is, based only on what one believes ought to be, or what isn’t is based on what one believes ought not to be.

This is the opposite of the *[naturalistic fallacy](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Naturalistic-Fallacy)*.

In his 1957 paper, Edward C. Moore defined the *moralistic fallacy* as the assertion that moral judgments are of a different order from factual judgements. Over the years, this concept has been simplified to deriving an “is” from an “ought.”

examples.example:
Being mean to others is wrong.

Therefore, it cannot possibly be part of our nature.
examples.explanation: While, morally speaking, being mean to others may be wrong, this has no bearing on the biological aspect of the desire or need. Again, what we shouldn’t do (according to moral norms), is not necessarily the same as what we are biologically influenced to do.

exceptions:
An argument can certainly be made that an ought is the same as an is, but it just cannot be assumed.

**Fun Fact:** The *naturalistic* and the *moralistic* fallacies are often confused with the *[appeal to nature](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Appeal-to-Nature)* fallacy. One reason, perhaps, is because what is “natural” is another way of saying what is, is. But with the *naturalistic* and the *moralistic* fallacies, the conclusion does not have to be based on what is “natural;” it just has to be based on what is. For example,

Men and women ought to be equal. Therefore, women are just as strong as men and men are just as empathetic as women.

This is another example of the *moralistic fallacy* but not an *[appeal to nature](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Appeal-to-Nature)*.
references: Moore, E. C. (1957). The Moralistic Fallacy. *The Journal of Philosophy*, 54(2), 29–42. https://doi.org/10.2307/2022356
Pinker, S. (2003). *The Blank Slate: The Modern Denial of Human Nature*. Penguin.
description_et:
Kui järeldus väljendab seda, mis on, põhineb ainult sellel, mis tema arvates peaks olema, või see, mis ei ole, sellel, mis tema arvates ei peaks olema.

See on *[naturalistliku eksituse](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Naturalistic-Fallacy)* vastand.

Edward C. Moore defineeris oma 1957. aasta artiklis *moralistlikku eksitust* kui väidet, et moraaliotsused erinevad faktilistest hinnangutest. Aastate jooksul on seda mõistet lihtsustatud, et tuletada sõna "on" sõnast "peaks".
exceptions_et:
Kindlasti võib väita, et peaks olema sama mis on, kuid seda lihtsalt ei saa eeldada.

**Lõbus fakt:** *naturalistlikku* ja *moralistlikku* ekslikkust aetakse sageli segi *[looduse poole pöördumisega](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Appeal-to-Nature)*. Üks põhjus võib olla selles, et see, mis on "loomulik", on teine ​​viis öelda, mis on, on. Kuid *naturalistlike* ja *moralistlike* eksimuste puhul ei pea järeldus põhinema sellel, mis on „loomulik”; see lihtsalt peab põhinema sellel, mis on. Näiteks

Mehed ja naised peaksid olema võrdsed. Seetõttu on naised täpselt sama tugevad kui mehed ja mehed on sama empaatilised kui naised.

See on veel üks näide *moralistlikust eksimusest*, kuid mitte *[looduse poole pöördumisest](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Appeal-to-Nature)*.

examples_et.example:
Teiste vastu kuri olla on vale.

Seetõttu ei saa see kuidagi olla osa meie olemusest.
examples_et.explanation: Kuigi moraalselt võib teiste vastu kuri olla vale, ei mõjuta see soovi või vajaduse bioloogilist aspekti. Jällegi, see, mida me ei peaks tegema (vastavalt moraalinormidele), ei pruugi olla sama, mis meid bioloogiliselt mõjutatakse.
